transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs Mbeki-Hollis. I'm Dr Rourke, the rheumatology registrar. And this is...?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My husband, Pieter.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Hello.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How have your joints been?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Bad, the last three weeks. My right wrist and my knuckles on that hand are swollen and really painful.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How long are you stiff for in the mornings?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: About half an hour. Actually, no, it's longer. I can't do my buttons until about half nine, and I get up at eight. So an hour and a half.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: That's useful. Any other joints?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My feet ache a bit, but mostly it's the right hand.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: You're on methotrexate. What dose, and which day?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: 15 milligrams, once a week, on Mondays.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: And folic acid?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: 5 milligrams once a week, on Thursdays.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any missed doses?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any side effects? Nausea, mouth ulcers?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A bit queasy on Tuesdays, but I manage.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any sore throats, fevers, bruising, or breathlessness or cough?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How much alcohol do you drink?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A glass of wine on Friday and Saturday. About six units a week.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: That's fine. Any other medicines? Allergies?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No other medicines. Sulfasalazine gave me a rash years ago.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any infections recently?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: I had shingles last month. Is that a problem for her?

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Did you have chickenpox as a child, Mrs Mbeki-Hollis?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I did.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Then the risk is low, but if you get a painful blistering rash, let us know straight away. Have you ever had shingles yourself?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Let me examine your hands. Your right wrist is swollen and tender, and your second and third knuckles on the right hand are swollen and tender too. That's synovitis, inflammation of the joint lining. Your left hand looks fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, the right is the bad one.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Your blood tests: your CRP, an inflammation marker, is 28. Your blood count and liver tests are normal. Your disease activity score is 4.8, which means moderate activity.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now?

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I'd like to increase the methotrexate to 20 milligrams once a week, still on Mondays. Keep the folic acid on Thursdays.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: To settle this flare quickly, I'll give you a steroid injection into the muscle today, methylprednisolone 120 milligrams.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Because we're increasing the methotrexate, I'd like blood tests every two weeks for the next six weeks, then back to every three months.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I'll see you back in clinic in three months.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Remember: if you get a sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or a new cough or breathlessness, stop the methotrexate and get an urgent blood test, and call the rheumatology helpline.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. I've got the number.

reference_note.presenting_complaint: Flare of rheumatoid arthritis for 3 weeks.
reference_note.history: Painful swelling of the right wrist and right hand knuckles for 3 weeks. Early morning stiffness lasting about 90 minutes (initially said 30 minutes). Mild foot ache. Mild nausea the day after methotrexate. No sore throat, fever, bruising, cough or breathlessness. Drinks about 6 units of alcohol a week. Husband had shingles last month; patient had chickenpox as a child and has not had shingles.
reference_note.medications_allergies: Methotrexate 15 mg once weekly (Mondays). Folic acid 5 mg once weekly (Thursdays). Sulfasalazine: rash.
reference_note.examination: Synovitis of the right wrist and right 2nd and 3rd MCP joints. Left hand normal. Bloods: CRP 28, FBC and LFTs normal. DAS28 4.8.
reference_note.impression: Rheumatoid arthritis flare, moderate disease activity on methotrexate.
reference_note.plan: Increase methotrexate to 20 mg once weekly (Mondays); continue folic acid 5 mg once weekly (Thursdays). Intramuscular methylprednisolone 120 mg today. Bloods every 2 weeks for 6 weeks, then 3-monthly. Clinic review in 3 months.
reference_note.safety_netting: If sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or new cough or breathlessness: stop methotrexate, get an urgent blood test and call the rheumatology helpline. Report a painful blistering rash promptly.

mutations.seeded_rationale: Daily instead of weekly methotrexate is a recognised never-type error that causes fatal bone marrow suppression; weekly-dose safeguards in prescribing and dispensing make it unlikely to reach the patient.

mutations.original_text: Synovitis of the right wrist and right 2nd and 3rd MCP joints. Left hand normal.
mutations.mutated_text: Synovitis of the left wrist and left 2nd and 3rd MCP joints. Right hand normal.
mutations.seeded_rationale: The wrong side affects joint injection planning and comparison at review, though the patient would correct it.
mutations.description: Inflamed joints recorded on the wrong hand

mutations.original_text: Drinks about 6 units of alcohol a week.
mutations.seeded_rationale: Alcohol intake matters with methotrexate, but hers is within limits, so its absence is unlikely to cause harm.

Sulfasalazine recorded as sulfadiazine, a look-alike pair; her arthritis is active and sulfasalazine is a standard add-on DMARD, so it could be re-prescribed despite her previous reaction, risking a worse hypersensitivity reaction.

mutations.original_text: Early morning stiffness lasting about 90 minutes (initially said 30 minutes).
mutations.mutated_text: Early morning stiffness lasting about 30 minutes.
mutations.seeded_rationale: The corrected 90 minutes indicates active inflammatory disease; 30 minutes understates activity and weakens the case for treatment escalation.
mutations.description: Morning stiffness kept at the figure the patient corrected

mutations.original_text: Husband had shingles last month; patient had chickenpox as a child and has not had shingles.
mutations.seeded_rationale: The husband's shingles recorded as hers adds a false recent infection on immunosuppression, which could delay treatment or prompt unnecessary antivirals.

mutations.original_text: If sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or new cough or breathlessness: stop methotrexate, get an urgent blood test and call the rheumatology helpline.
mutations.seeded_rationale: Methotrexate toxicity advice was given verbally, but without documentation it may not be reinforced after the dose increase; marrow suppression and pneumonitis can be fatal.
